novel_features.name: Energy & cost rollup
novel_features.description: See total kWh and cost for your charging over any period, rolled up by month or by charger.
novel_features.rationale: The Zaptec portal only shows session-by-session; a monthly total requires aggregating the local session store, which no single API call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user asks how much they charged or what it cost over a period — it answers from local history instead of N paginated API calls.

novel_features.name: What's-charging-now snapshot
novel_features.description: One table showing every charger's mode (charging/connected/finished/offline) with decoded power, current, and phase.
novel_features.rationale: Joins synced charger rows with a live state fetch and decodes numeric observation IDs via the baked constants table — there is no portal or Home Assistant single-view equivalent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for an instant fleet status check instead of clicking through chargers one by one in the portal.

novel_features.name: Load-balancing headroom
novel_features.description: Show how many amps of the installation's breaker limit are uncommitted versus actively drawn.
novel_features.rationale: Subtracts decoded active per-charger draw from the installation's max available-current; operators otherwise tune the 15-minute-guarded limit blind.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before raising or lowering an installation's available current so the change is informed by real draw.

novel_features.name: Stale / offline charger watch
novel_features.description: List chargers that are offline, disconnected, or haven't reported within a threshold.
novel_features.rationale: A pure local query over synced charger/state rows; the Home Assistant integration polls but offers no offline alerting.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to catch dead or stuck chargers before a resident or driver complains.

novel_features.name: Firmware drift
novel_features.description: Group an installation's chargers by firmware version and flag the ones behind the fleet majority.
novel_features.rationale: Turns the raw firmware list into an upgrade decision by computing the modal version across the fleet locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before scheduling firmware upgrades to see which chargers actually need one.

novel_features.name: Session anomaly scan
novel_features.description: Flag charging sessions with near-zero energy, abnormally long duration, or zero cost.
novel_features.rationale: Threshold SQL over the local session table surfaces quality issues no incumbent tool reports.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to audit charging-session quality and catch stuck or mis-metered sessions.

narrative.headline: The only command-line tool for Zaptec Go chargers — pause and resume charging, read live state in plain English, and track energy and cost from a local database.
narrative.value_prop: Control and monitor your Zaptec charger from the terminal or a cron job, without opening the portal app or running Home Assistant. Decodes the API's numeric observation and command IDs for you, syncs your charging history into a local SQLite store, and answers questions the portal can't — like monthly kWh and cost rollups (cost), instant fleet status (live), and offline-charger detection (chargers stale).
narrative.auth_narrative: Zaptec uses OAuth2 password grant. Run `zaptec-pp-cli auth login` with your Zaptec portal username and password (or set ZAPTEC_USERNAME and ZAPTEC_PASSWORD); the CLI exchanges them for a bearer token at https://api.zaptec.com/oauth/token, caches it locally, and refreshes it when it expires.

quickstart.comment: Exchange your Zaptec username/password for a cached bearer token
Find your charger and copy its id
See decoded live state: mode, power, current, energy
Preview a pause command before sending it
Pull charging history into the local store for cost analytics
Monthly kWh and cost rollup the portal never shows

troubleshoots.fix: Run `zaptec-pp-cli auth login` again — the cached token expired or the credentials changed.
The API caps at 10 req/s per account; the client backs off automatically, but avoid tight loops over many chargers.

troubleshoots.symptom: current set refuses or warns about the 15-minute guard
troubleshoots.fix: Zaptec enforces a 15-minute minimum between installation available-current updates; wait or pass the override flag if you accept the risk.

troubleshoots.symptom: state shows raw numeric ids instead of names
troubleshoots.fix: Run `zaptec-pp-cli sync` (or `constants`) to refresh the baked decode tables from /api/constants.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs to inspect or control a Zaptec EV charger non-interactively: checking whether a car is charging, pausing or resuming charging in response to electricity prices, reading decoded charger telemetry, or answering energy and cost questions from charging history. It is the right tool whenever the task involves a Zaptec Go/Go2/Pro charger and a terminal or script rather than the phone app.

recipes.title: Pause charging when prices spike
recipes.explanation: Send a StopCharging command from a price-watching cron job; add --dry-run first to preview.

recipes.title: Monthly cost report
recipes.explanation: Roll up local session history into per-month kWh and cost totals as structured JSON.

recipes.title: Trim a verbose charger state
recipes.explanation: state returns decoded observation rows (state_id, name, value, unit); --select name,value keeps just the readable pairs so an agent doesn't carry the full payload.

recipes.title: Catch offline chargers
recipes.explanation: List chargers that haven't reported recently before a resident complains.

recipes.explanation: See which chargers are behind the fleet's majority firmware version before upgrading.
